claims.claim: The server key is sealed in OutLayer's keystore. It opens only for this contract running exactly release.wasm; no code path deletes or replaces it.
Before any sale an enclave decrypts the artifact with the escrowed key and confirms its build hash; only sha256(key) leaves it.
The licence contract has no access keys: nobody can redeploy it, drain it or delete it. v2 instances are born that way.
buy_licence takes the exact price and mints a NEP-171 token: 60% goes to the studio, 40% stays locked as that token's pot share.
Death by probes needs holder-signed sessions on the official server (a signed 200 is not enough) and K failures spaced in time. An OutLayer timeout is inconclusive, never a failure.
Holders can also kill it: a quorum of report_down calls inside the window, one per token. The studio can end service itself; nobody can keep it alive by saying so.

After death anyone can release: the enclave re-reads the contract, requires Dead, and outputs the key; the contract stores it publicly only if sha256(key) = the commitment. Released early is impossible.

Each holder takes a refund of their pot share or pledges it to the keep-alive pool, once. Sales after death put their price, net of mint storage, into the pool (v1: all of it; v2: 90%, with 10% to the gas-free ops budget).
A fan runs the released build and gets paid from the pool for unique holders served: pay = verified sessions x rate, capped, once per host and epoch, never below zero.
The fan-host CLI downloads the artifact from any mirror, refuses wrong bytes, and decrypts only with the key whose hash is on chain.

rehearsed_vs_real.detail: The judge instances run probe interval 20 s, 3 failures, windows 2 to 3 min, epoch 2 min so a lifecycle fits a video. The contract code is identical; production defaults (6 h, 4 failures, 72 h windows, 7-day epochs) are init config, listed in the README. No production-length run was done.

We deleted our own Cloudflare Worker (`scripts/ops/kill-official.sh`). What followed is real contract state: failed probes spaced in time, then Dead, then release. We chose the moment; the contract decided the rest.

Ember Rift is a fictional studio title. The studio account, the four player accounts and the fan host are all ours, on testnet. The community server is the released build running for real, hosted by us in the fan role.

UI flows in the film were driven from a local build with a localhost-only test-account signer (no wallet keys imported anywhere). Every transaction they sent is on testnet and listed above. Wallet sign-in through Meteor or MyNearWallet was not exercised end to end.
NEAR testnet and Base Sepolia. Nothing has real value. Base Sepolia payouts are demo-sized (10^13 wei per verified session, 0.00001 ETH).

The NEAR MPC signer `v1.signer-prod.testnet` signs the payout transactions; the contract verifies the signature recovers to its derived address before storing it. The Base Sepolia receipts are public.

Zero-deposit calls are paid from the contract's ops budget (seeded by us, topped up by 10% of post-death sales). The relayer (Cloudflare Pages) pays gas only and is ours: a holder who distrusts it can send the same call and pay gas themselves.

Walrus testnet is not permanent storage and is wiped periodically. It is one mirror of three; the studio's copy and GitHub raw serve the same hash-pinned bytes, and any single honest mirror is enough.

release.wasm and probe.wasm (the code the escrow trusts) rebuild bit-for-bit in OutLayer's pinned compiler image. The licence wasm is cargo plus wasm-opt from a local toolchain and is not claimed to be bit-reproducible; its identity is its hash and its public on-chain bytes.

The v2 judge instance's bundle is attested by a public GitHub Actions workflow (Sigstore, Rekor). v1 and the dev instance predate that pipeline: their build hash is checked by decrypting the released artifact instead.

The key opens only in OutLayer's TEE workers (Intel TDX) under a keystore whose master key comes from NEAR MPC. We prove the rule we asked the keystore to enforce (the store_secrets call on chain), not the enclave's honesty.
